name: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd
title: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd - 543300 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹12,310 crore (+54% YoY) and BEV revenue +107%, but EBITDA margin fell to 23.1% on input inflation and pass-through lag; capex and capacity not discussed.

triggers.label: EBITDA margin 23.1% on input costs
triggers.quote: Margins were heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases as well as the timing gap in the customer recoveries or the pass-throughs.

triggers.label: BEV revenue +107% YoY
triggers.quote: BEV revenue grew 107% despite EV demand in the US remaining weak.

triggers.label: Denso JVs: high-voltage and 2W/3W
triggers.quote: The first will focus on high voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for 4 and 4+ wheel vehicles

guidance.value: Recovery measures more visible from Q2
guidance.quote: We expect that these recovery measures will become progressively more visible from quarter 2 onwards.

red_flags.label: Margin compression from input costs and pass-through lag
red_flags.quote: This, along with the arithmetic impact on both revenue and cost, may continue to create some pressure on margin as a percentage.

evasions.topic: JV2 SOP timeline and revenue start
evasions.quote: The SOP timelines, unfortunately, Pramod, we are restricted by confidentiality agreements on it
This is a question about a different company who's our partner, and they should be answering it, not us.

summary.headline: Sona Comstar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23.1% on input-cost inflation and pass-through lag.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore, with BEV revenue up 107% to ₹436 crore and BEV share of automotive sales at 44%, both described as the best ever. EBITDA rose 49% to ₹303 crore but margin contracted about 0.7 pp to 23.1%, with April and May weak and June better on pass-through recoveries. PAT grew 45% to ₹181 crore (13.6% margin). Management framed the quarter alongside the Denso JV announcement (two JVs: high-voltage/hybrid for 4W and 2/3W electrification) and a new Robotics and Physical AI vertical with ₹800 crore order book.

financial_highlights.metric: BEV share of automotive product sales

segments.name: Electrification (BEV)
segments.commentary: BEV revenue ₹436 crore, +107% YoY, highest ever BEV mix; EV order book at 69 programmes across 36 customers after 2 new EV and 1 hybrid programme.

segments.name: Traction motors / suspension motors
segments.commentary: Traction motors had the fastest growth in the quarter along with EV suspension motors (management ranked suspension motors fastest in growth); traction motors carry lowest margin and diluted group margin.

segments.name: Driveline / ICE differential gears
segments.commentary: Won ₹2.1 billion ICE differential gear programme from a North American OEM; new hybrid differential assembly order from an existing North American customer.

segments.name: Robotics and Physical AI
segments.commentary: Three new orders adding ₹6 billion, taking the vertical's order book to ₹8 billion; first product (AMR) prototype shown at CES; one SOP in Q1 FY28 per management timing guidance.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Railway acquisition in first year of post-acquisition integration; additional railway business wins noted, no revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Margin recovery expected to become progressively more visible from Q2 FY27 as cost pass-throughs catch up; June showed significant improvement over April-May.
Management said material-cost pass-through lag and revenue/cost arithmetic may keep pressure on margin percentage in the near term.
Expects phenomenal EV growth in India and Europe-led electrification to continue through the year, though US EV demand is weak.
Robotics orders: one SOP this quarter, one next quarter, one within 15 months; management said the market is developing faster than internal assumptions.
JV2 (high voltage) SOP timeline not disclosed due to confidentiality; JV1 expected to kick off faster than JV2.
capex_capacity: Management said it has no capacity constraint; OEM constraints are supply-chain driven, and capacity is built ahead of markets.
Denso JV2 (high voltage 4W/CV electrification) is Denso majority-owned with Denso leading management; JV1 (2/3W) is Sona majority-owned with Sona management control and licenses technology to the JV.
Management cited capex intensity thumb rule of ₹8-9 revenue per ₹1 capex for high-voltage systems, and at least ₹11-12 per ₹1 capex per Sat Mohan Gupta.
Suspension, motor and non-traction motor businesses are outside the Denso JV scope.
Robotics products under commercialisation include short-range radar sensors and advanced robotic components; AMR platform in development.
demand_pricing: Demand healthy across markets: India strong (passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers), Europe growing, US improved through the quarter, China mixed but fastest-growing geography for the company due to suspension motor ramp-up.
Management said EV volumes are constrained by OEM supply chains rather than demand.
Input cost inflation (commodities, labour) was the main margin headwind; April and May were tough, June improved.
Rare earth: heavy rare earth magnets remain restricted from import; company has shifted to light rare earth alternatives with no magnet shortage for traction motors.
Management described high-voltage motor competition as less intense than 2/3W due to technology barriers.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about AI/robotics economics, software share of value, and capital commitment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said metal plus software is now standard across products; suspension motors carry 2 million lines of code. Robotics entry has three revenue streams: components, perception engineering services, and full platforms (AMRs and cobots); no capex guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for JV2 revenue and capacity/TAM sizing for high-voltage JV?
qa_highlights.answer: SOP timelines withheld under confidentiality; JV1 to lead and JV2 to follow. Denso electrification revenue above $8 billion a year; Indian hybrid/EV car and CV addressable market ~2.3 million vehicles, about ₹24,000 crore by 2030 and roughly 3x that by 2035 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why put 2/3W traction motors into JV1 when already growing well?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Denso's interest, access to customers currently not open, export opportunities where Denso is dominant, and a single strategic intent across both JVs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-axle in JV1 but not JV2?
qa_highlights.answer: JV2 makes motors and inverters; e-axle (motor, inverter, gearbox integration) is a tiny market for JV1 and can be sold to e-axle makers, OEMs, or Sona driveline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is VA-to-employee ratio declining QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to product mix shift toward assembly businesses (motors, railways) vs driveline; ratio at 4.5x is still strong and varies quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When do robotics orders start production?
qa_highlights.answer: One starts this quarter, one next quarter, and one within about 15 months; most within 12-15 months.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery: whether EBITDA margin improvement from pass-through shows in Q2 FY27 as management guided.
Traction motor mix: lowest-margin product growing fastest, a continuing dilution to group margin.
Execution risk on Denso JV1 and JV2: SOP timing not disclosed; capex and royalty economics not quantified.
Robotics: early-stage, ₹8 billion order book, product life cycles and generational change unclear to management as well.
Rare earth magnet restriction on heavy rare earths; company relies on light rare earth alternatives.
US EV demand weakness and OEM supply-chain bottlenecks limiting volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, electrification and new partnerships; cautious on near-term margins, explicitly attributing pressure to input inflation and pass-through lag. Evasive on JV timelines, JV2 revenue sizing and Denso's own India supply, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: I'm happy to share this was the best ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue, and BEV revenue share, with very healthy momentum, continuing across the business.
Margins were heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases as well as the timing gap in the customer recoveries or the pass-throughs.
EV is in a way, right now, we are not constrained by demand. Actually, all our OEMs are not constrained by demand. They are constrained by their own supply chain challenges.
Our suspension motor product has 2 million lines of code. Almost nothing we make today is just metal, it is metal and a few lines of code.
Denso is not a leader, it is by far the runaway leader when it comes to hybrid powertrains. The electrification business revenue for Denso is above $8 billion a year.
